saints.name: Saint Paisios of Mount Athos
saints.title: Saint Paisios of Mount Athos, Athonite Elder
saints.notes: Elder Paisios Eznepidis (1924–1994) was one of the most beloved Athonite monks of the 20th century, renowned for his gifts of discernment, prophecy, and healing. Born in Cappadocia, he spent decades on Mount Athos and Sinai offering spiritual counsel to thousands of pilgrims. Canonized in 2015 by the Holy and Sacred Synod of the Ecumenical Patriarchate.

saints.name: Saint Porphyrios of Kafsokalivia
saints.title: Saint Porphyrios of Kafsokalivia, Elder of the Holy Mountain
saints.notes: Elder Porphyrios Bairaktaris (1906–1991) was an Athonite elder venerated for extraordinary gifts of spiritual perception, healing, and love. He spent years in the Kafsokalivia skete and later founded the Convent of the Transfiguration in Milesi, Athens. Canonized in 2013 by the Ecumenical Patriarchate.

saints.name: Saint Kosmas of Aetolia
saints.title: Saint Kosmas of Aetolia, Equal-to-the-Apostles and New Martyr
saints.notes: Cosmas of Aetolia (1714–1779), monk of Mount Athos, became a tireless missionary throughout Greece, Albania, and the Balkans. He founded hundreds of schools and churches, teaching in villages and preaching Christian values. Martyred by hanging in 1779. Glorified as Equal-to-the-Apostles by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 1961.

saints.name: Saint Nektarios of Aegina
saints.title: Saint Nektarios of Pentapolis, Wonder-worker of Aegina
saints.notes: Nektarios Kephalas (1846–1920), Metropolitan of Pentapolis, was unjustly exiled from Alexandria and endured years of slander and poverty before being vindicated. He founded the Convent of the Holy Trinity on Aegina, where he died. Known for countless posthumous miracles. Canonized in 1961 by the Ecumenical Patriarchate.

saints.name: Saint Iakovos of Evia
saints.title: Saint Iakovos Tsalikis of Evia, Venerable Elder
saints.notes: Elder Iakovos Tsalikis (1920–1991) was abbot of the Monastery of Saint David of Evia, Greece, a man of deep asceticism and wonder-working prayer. He bore invisible stigmata and was gifted with clairvoyance and healing. He tirelessly cared for pilgrims and the sick. Canonized in 1997 by the Holy and Sacred Synod of the Ecumenical Patriarchate.
